copy.blurb:
FIFA World Cup 2026 on Friday, evening UTC kickoff, brings Norway and France together. The Desk's read disagrees with the market on the France side, by +17.7pp — and that disagreement is the Pick.

On Elo, France comes in 270 points ahead — Norway at 1760, France at 2030. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Norway to win at 15%, the draw at 14%, and France to win at 71%. The Desk's three-way distribution is calibrated against the W/D/L resolution Polymarket and Kalshi settle on, not against the exact scoreline. France sits at 71% of the mass.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Norway to win at 20%, the draw at 24%, and France to win at 54%. On the France side specifically the market reads 54%, which prices out at American odds of −115. Compared against the model's 71%, that's the +17.7pp gap the Pick rests on.

Pick gate is a lower-bound check, not the point estimate. A 100-sample bootstrap perturbs the Elo prior (±20), the host bonus (±15), and the altitude bonus (±10), then reads the 5th-percentile probability back out. On the France side that lower bound is 64% — +10.3pp clear of the market's 54%, comfortably past our +3pp threshold. Calibration tracks the closing market on the bulk sample; selection — picking the single side where the gap is wide — is where the engine's edge has to come from. This verdict is a selection call on the France side.

This number will move. Confirmed starting elevens, injuries, weather at the venue, and suspensions carried in from previous fixtures all re-enter the prior on the late-binding cadence. With kickoff roughly 35 days out, the model is on the weekly refresh cadence; we'll move to daily once we cross the T-5d window. The Pick can flip to a Pass if news moves enough of the prior. The Desk does not tip and does not recommend a trade — the model price, the market price, and the gap across them are what's on the page.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives France a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +17.7pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.

copy.summary: On every meaningful read, France look stronger here than Polymarket has them. Model 71% vs market 54% — a +17.7pp gap on the favourite side.
copy.title: Norway v France · the model leans France
